title: Noop repository update should skip verification

timeline.message:
Noop repository update should skip verification

It is common to do an idempotent PUT of a repo, just to ensure it is
there. This commit ensures that if the change is in fact a noop change,
we no longer do any repository verification, since a node having trouble
(for instance running out of heap) could then mean such a no-change
repo update failing.

Closes #76012
timeline.author: Henning Andersen

How does this verify that no verification takes place?

reply.body:
The new node does not share the same `path.repo` as the rest of the cluster and therefore fails verification. The PUT would fail if it did any verification, thus checking that the verification does not run.

I added a bit more to the comment to explain this.
Ah thanks, sorry for being slow there :) Sweet idea for a test :)

Yeah, thanks, that can work out. I did consider it, but were somewhat afraid of one of:

1. `canUpdateInPlace` sometime in the future allowing `type` update too in certain cases.
2. `canUpdateInPlace` returning false due to a repo-plugin that returns false even if the settings are identical.

I was probably over-thinking this so went with your suggestion, 1 would need some change in those lines anyway and 2 would be a bug in the repo plugin.
